ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The cross-section of a certain transparent medium is shown in the figure. $BC$ is a quarter-circle arc with radius $R$, $o$ is the center, and △AOC is a right triangle with $\angle O A C=60^{\circ}$. $A B$ is perpendicular to a sufficiently large screen $M N$, and point $A$ is in contact with the screen $M N$. A thin beam of light is directed along the radius of the arc toward the center $o$. When the angle of incidence $i=60^{\circ}$ at the interface $A B$, only a single bright spot is formed on the screen $M N$, assuming no multiple reflections of light within the transparent medium are considered.

1. What should the refractive index of the medium be not less than?
2. If $n=\sqrt{3}$, when the angle of incidence $i$ gradually decreases to $i_{0}$, the light spot on the right side of point $A$ just disappears, and there is only a light spot on the left side of point $A$ on the screen. What are $i_{0}$ and the distance from the light spot to point $A$?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the left boundary AB of the transparent medium is a vertical line, the top MN is a horizontal screen, point A is on the screen MN, and AB is perpendicular to the screen. O is on AB, and a dashed line passes horizontally through O; the right boundary BC is a quarter circular arc centered at O; C is to the right of O, A, O, and C form a right triangle, and AC is an inclined straight boundary. The incident ray travels toward O along the radius direction of the circular arc, so it is incident along the normal at the circular arc, does not change direction, and then reaches AB; the figure marks its angle of incidence i with the horizontal normal direction. Reasoning: Set coordinates according to the specified method: take O=(0,0), AB as the vertical direction, MN as the horizontal direction, and C=(R,0). Since the radius of BC is R, OC=R. △AOC is a right triangle and ∠OAC=60°, so OA=R/√3, therefore A=(0,R/√3). The slope of line AC is (0-R/√3)/(R-0)=-1/√3, that is, AC makes an angle of -30° with the horizontal line; the normal direction of AC makes an angle of 60° with the horizontal line. Question 1: When i=60°, the reflected light at AB can continue to propagate inside the medium and finally form the right-side light spot. The problem states that there is only one bright spot on the screen, indicating that no refracted light exits at AB to the left-side screen anymore, that is, total reflection occurs at AB. The critical angle from the medium to air satisfies sin i_c=1/n. For total reflection at i=60°, 60°≥i_c is needed, that is, sin60°≥1/n, so n≥1/sin60°=2/√3=2√3/3. Question 2: Let n=√3. After reflection at AB, the light ray in the medium still makes angle i with the horizontal line and travels toward AC. From the geometric relation, the normal of AC makes an angle of 60° with the horizontal line, so the incidence angle when this ray reaches AC is α=60°−i. When the right-side light spot just disappears, the light refracted out at AC is exactly along the horizontal direction, that is, the refraction angle relative to the normal of AC is 60°. From Snell's law n sinα=sin60°, we get √3 sin(60°−i0)=sin60°=√3/2, hence sin(60°−i0)=1/2. Take the solution consistent with the gradual decrease process, 60°−i0=30°, so i0=30°. At this time, there is still emergent light at AB directed toward the left-side screen. Apply Snell's law to the AB interface: sin r=n sin i0=√3·sin30°=√3/2, so r=60°, where r is the angle of the emergent light relative to the horizontal normal of AB. The vertical distance from A to O is OA=R/√3. After the emergent light exits from O and reaches the horizontal screen MN, its horizontal displacement is OA/tan60°=(R/√3)/√3=R/3. Therefore the distance from the left-side light spot to A is R/3.
